problem: A school bus collected 38 children at its first stop. At the next stop, 27 more children climbed on. How many children are riding the bus now?
follow_up_questions: At the third stop, 19 children get off. How many children remain on the bus?
The bus has seats for 80 children. How many seats could still be filled?

problem: How many shoppers are inside the market hall if 38 came in when the doors opened and another 27 wandered in a little later?
follow_up_questions: Later, 19 shoppers head home with their bags. How many are still inside?
The hall holds 80 shoppers at most. How many more could fit inside?

problem: At the school book fair, children bought 13 comic books, 11 atlases and 18 storybooks. The fair was held in the gym. How many books were sold?
follow_up_questions: Every book sold came with 2 bookmarks. How many bookmarks were handed out?
The fair started with 95 bookmarks. How many bookmarks are left?
Then the organisers open 4 packets holding 9 bookmarks each. How many bookmarks do they have now?

problem: Find the total number of plants sold at the garden centre's spring sale, where customers took home 13 rose bushes, 11 lemon trees and 18 tomato plants. Soft music played in the greenhouse all day.
follow_up_questions: Each plant was sold with 2 plant labels. How many labels were given away?
The centre had 95 labels before the sale. How many labels remain?
The manager then unpacks 4 bundles of 9 labels. How many labels are there now?

problem: The science fair filled two rooms, with 23 projects in the gym and 28 in the library. How many projects were on show?
follow_up_questions: Each project got a score from 2 judges. How many scores were given in all?

problem: What was the total number of swimmers at the gala if 23 raced in the junior heats and 28 raced in the senior heats?
follow_up_questions: Every swimmer swam 2 lengths of the pool. How many lengths were swum altogether?

problem: On a ferry, 34 travellers stood at the front rail and 29 stood at the back rail. How many travellers were out on deck?
follow_up_questions: When it grew windy, 18 travellers went inside. How many stayed on deck?
The travellers left on deck gathered in groups of 5 for photos. How many groups were there?

problem: A campsite has tents in two spots: 29 in the woods and 34 beside the lake. Find how many tents there are at the campsite.
follow_up_questions: In the morning, 18 tents are packed up. How many tents are still standing?
A ranger can inspect 5 tents an hour. How many hours will she need to inspect all the standing tents?

problem: A florist ordered 48 tulips and 67 daisies for a wedding. How many flowers did she order?
How many crayons are in the art cupboard altogether if one tub holds 48 red crayons and another tub holds 67 blue crayons?
There were 48 frogs sitting on lily pads in a pond. A heron landed nearby, and 29 frogs jumped into the water. How many frogs are still on the lily pads?
follow_up_questions: A little later, 13 frogs climbed back up. How many frogs are on the lily pads now?

problem: When the bell rang, 29 of the 48 children in the playground went inside. How many children stayed out in the playground?
follow_up_questions: A few minutes later, 13 children ran back out to fetch their coats. How many are in the playground now?

problem: Mrs. Okafor kept 44 sheets of coloured paper in a folder. Her class used 32 of them to make paper lanterns. How many sheets remain in the folder?
follow_up_questions: She buys a pack of 30 more sheets. How many sheets are in the folder now?
Each group of children needs 6 sheets for a mural. How many groups can get sheets?

problem: How many birthday candles does Lars have left? He began with a box of 44 candles and put 32 of them on his grandmother's cake.
follow_up_questions: He picks up another box of 30 candles. How many candles does he have now?
He ties the candles in bundles of 6. How many bundles can he make?

problem: A library had 37 laptops on its charging cart in the morning. By lunchtime only 12 were still on the cart, since students had borrowed the others. How many laptops were borrowed?
Out of the 37 rowing boats at the lake, just 12 were tied up at the dock by afternoon. The rest were out on the water. Find how many boats were out on the water.
A garden centre began the spring with 84 bags of soil. When the season was over, 19 bags were left. How many bags were sold?
follow_up_questions: Each bag sold for 3 dollars. How much money did the bags of soil bring in?

problem: How many raffle tickets did the club sell at the fair if it printed 84 tickets and had 19 left over at the end?
follow_up_questions: Every ticket cost 3 dollars. How much money did the club raise from them?

problem: The music room keeps 35 recorders in a cupboard. The teacher lends 16 of them to the choir. How many recorders are still in the cupboard?
follow_up_questions: The choir gives 9 recorders back. How many recorders are in the cupboard now?
The recorders are placed on 4 shelves, with the same number on each shelf. How many recorders sit on each shelf?
Each shelf also holds 3 songbooks. How many songbooks are on the shelves?

problem: A bike rental stand owns 35 bikes, but 16 of them are out on a school trip. What number of bikes is still at the stand?
follow_up_questions: Later, 9 of the rented bikes come back. How many bikes are at the stand now?
The bikes are parked in 4 equal rows. How many bikes are in each row?
Every row also has 3 helmets hanging beside it. How many helmets is that?

problem: A school kitchen made 70 sandwiches for a field trip. By mid-morning, 45 had been handed out. How many sandwiches were still on the tray?
follow_up_questions: The cook packs the leftover sandwiches into bags of 5. How many bags does she fill?

problem: How many carrots did Grandpa keep after giving 45 of the 70 carrots he grew to the neighbours?
follow_up_questions: He ties the carrots he kept into bunches of 5. How many bunches does he make?

problem: A farmer picked 34 melons for the weekend market. The morning was foggy and cool. He gave 16 of the melons to the school kitchen. How many melons did he keep for the market?
Find the number of jars of jam still in Grandma Elif's pantry. She made 34 jars this summer and has given 16 jars to her friends. Her kitchen smells of strawberries all day.
A tennis coach had 76 balls in a bin. She lent 65 of them to the summer camp. How many tennis balls are still in her bin?
follow_up_questions: She buys 4 tubes of new balls with 6 balls in each tube. How many balls does she have now?
Five players share these balls equally. How many balls does each player get?

problem: There were 76 paintbrushes in the art room until 65 were sent off to the community mural project. What is the number of paintbrushes left in the art room?
follow_up_questions: Then 4 new packs arrive, each with 6 brushes. How many brushes are in the art room now?
The brushes are shared equally among five tables. How many brushes go to each table?

problem: A gardener had 72 tulip bulbs and planted 47 of them in the park. How many bulbs does she still have?
follow_up_questions: She puts each bulb she still has in its own pot, with 4 scoops of soil per pot. How many scoops of soil does she need?

problem: How many seashells are left in Kai's collection after he trades 47 of his 72 shells with a friend?
follow_up_questions: He glues each shell he kept onto a card with 4 drops of glue. How many drops of glue does he use?

problem: A football coach owned 92 practice cones. He donated 53 to the youth league. How many cones does he still own?
follow_up_questions: He orders a new set of 25 cones. How many cones does he have now?

problem: What is left of Ravi's 92 trading cards after he gives 53 away to his younger cousins?
follow_up_questions: His aunt gives him a pack of 25 new cards. How many cards does he have now?

problem: A bookshop had 61 copies of a new dinosaur book. A library bought 48 copies for its reading program. How many copies are still at the bookshop?
follow_up_questions: The bookshop orders 2 boxes with 15 copies in each. How many copies will it have once they arrive?
Over the following days it sells 27 copies. How many copies are left?

problem: Of the 61 helmets at the ice rink, 48 were rented out for a birthday party. How many helmets are still on the shelf?
follow_up_questions: The rink receives 2 cartons with 15 helmets in each. How many helmets will be on the shelf after the delivery?
During the next few days, 27 helmets get rented. How many remain?

problem: When the fair closed, Ms. Duarte still had 36 jars of honey on her table. She had started the day with 95 jars. How many jars did she sell?
follow_up_questions: Each jar sold for 4 dollars. How much money did she collect?
She paid 50 dollars for her table space. How much money did she have left after paying?
She splits that money equally among the three beekeepers who helped her. How much does each beekeeper get?

problem: How many loaves did a baker sell at the street market if he arrived with 95 loaves and went home with 36?
follow_up_questions: He charged 4 dollars per loaf. How much money did he make?
The market fee was 50 dollars. How much money was left after he paid it?
He divides that money equally among three helpers. What is each helper's share?

problem: A farm stand had 74 ears of corn in a crate. After the morning shoppers came through, only 18 ears were left. How many ears did the shoppers buy?
Only 18 balloons were left at the end of the parade, but the clowns had started out with 74. How many balloons did the clowns give away?
Aunt Sofia had 84 dollars after paying for a train ticket. At the bookshop she then spent 17 dollars on a cookbook. How much money does she have now?
follow_up_questions: Next she buys 3 greeting cards at 2 dollars each. How much money does she have left?

problem: How much money is left in Omar's wallet? He had 84 dollars once his groceries were paid for, then paid 17 dollars for a haircut.
follow_up_questions: Afterwards he buys 3 newspapers for 2 dollars each. How much is in his wallet now?

problem: Before the school book fair, Diego had 46 dollars in his wallet. He bought presents for his sisters there, and after that he had 29 dollars left. The gym was full of colourful posters. How much did he spend on presents?
follow_up_questions: He also paid 3 dollars for gift wrapping. How much did the presents and wrapping cost together?
How much money did he have after paying for the wrapping?

problem: Find how much Mrs. Lindqvist paid for the zoo tickets. She had 46 dollars when she reached the gate and 29 dollars once the tickets were bought. The penguins were being fed as they walked in.
follow_up_questions: She also bought a map for 3 dollars. How much did the tickets and map cost altogether?
How much money did she have once she had paid for the map?

problem: A pair of football boots is priced at 42 dollars, but the sports shop is taking 15 dollars off this weekend. What do the boots cost this weekend?
follow_up_questions: Kenji pays for the boots with two 20-dollar notes. How much change does he receive?
He then spends 8 dollars of his change on football socks. How much money does he have left?

problem: How much does a board game cost during the sale if its usual price is 42 dollars and the shop knocks 15 dollars off?
follow_up_questions: Selin hands the cashier two 20-dollar notes. How much change should she get back?
With her change she buys a deck of cards for 8 dollars. How much money remains?

problem: The Owls won the spelling bowl with 74 points. Our team finished 19 points behind them, even though we had practised for 6 weeks. What was our score?
follow_up_questions: We then answered a bonus question worth 12 points. What is our new total?

problem: How many points did the Tigers score in the basketball final? The Lions, who won, scored 74 points, and the Tigers lost by 19. The match was played in front of 85 fans.
follow_up_questions: In a shootout game afterwards, the Tigers added 12 points. What is their new total?

problem: In the school spelling contest, Ahmed scored 64 points and Grace scored 47. How many points ahead of Grace was Ahmed?
follow_up_questions: In the second round, Grace scored 9 points more than in her first. What was her second-round score?
How many points behind Ahmed's score is her second-round score?

problem: Ola and Mateus entered a diving contest. The judges gave Ola 64 points and Mateus 47 points. What was the difference between their scores?
follow_up_questions: Mateus dived again and scored 9 points more than on his first dive. What did his second dive score?
How many points short of Ola's score was his second dive?

problem: The Red House won the school sports day with 81 points, which was 26 points more than the Blue House. How many points did the Blue House get?
Find the score of Team Comet in the science quiz if Team Rocket won with 81 points and was 26 points ahead of Team Comet.
Hana grew a sunflower 92 centimetres tall. It was 15 centimetres taller than her friend Leo's sunflower. How tall is Leo's sunflower?
follow_up_questions: Leo's sunflower grows another 8 centimetres. How tall is it now?

problem: How tall is the shorter sandcastle? Marco's sandcastle stands 92 centimetres high, which is 15 centimetres higher than his cousin's.
follow_up_questions: His cousin adds a tower 8 centimetres tall to the top. What is the cousin's sandcastle's height now?

problem: The museum had 93 visitors on Monday and only 68 on Tuesday. How many fewer visitors came on Tuesday?
follow_up_questions: On Wednesday, 14 more visitors came than on Tuesday. How many visitors came on Wednesday?
What is the total for Tuesday and Wednesday?
Of those Tuesday and Wednesday visitors, 37 were children. How many were adults?

problem: By how much did the number of swimmers at the pool drop from morning to afternoon, if 93 people swam in the morning and 68 in the afternoon?
follow_up_questions: In the evening, 14 more people swam than in the afternoon. How many people swam in the evening?
How many swam in the afternoon and evening altogether?
Of the afternoon and evening swimmers, 37 were children. How many were adults?

problem: At the car wash, Bao dried 53 cars and Freya dried 38. The sun was shining all afternoon. How many more cars did Bao dry than Freya?
follow_up_questions: After her break, Freya dries 21 more cars. What is her count now?
By how many cars is Freya now ahead of Bao?

problem: How many more birdhouses did Ezra paint than Nia? At the craft fair, Ezra painted 53 birdhouses and Nia painted 38. A small dog slept under their table.
follow_up_questions: Later, Nia paints 21 more. How many has she painted now?
By how many birdhouses does Nia now lead Ezra?

problem: The red kite rose to 85 metres, which was 39 metres higher than the green kite. How high did the green kite fly?
follow_up_questions: With a longer string, the green kite flies twice as high. How high does it fly now?

problem: How tall is the old oak tree in the park? The pine tree beside it is 85 feet tall, 39 feet taller than the oak.
follow_up_questions: A tree on the hill is twice as tall as the oak. How tall is that tree?

problem: On a camping trip, a family packed 95 crackers and ate 57 of them on the first night. They slept in a tent for 8 people. How many crackers are still packed?
follow_up_questions: On the second night they eat 19 more. How many crackers are left?
Dad buys a box of 24 crackers at the camp store. How many crackers does the family have now?

problem: How many juice boxes are left in the cooler? The coach of the under-8 team filled it with 95 juice boxes, and the players drank 57 at half-time.
follow_up_questions: After the match they drink 19 more. How many juice boxes are left now?
A parent brings a pack of 24 juice boxes. How many juice boxes are in the cooler now?

problem: At breakfast, Mina had read 28 pages of her new book. By bedtime she had read 73 pages in all. How many pages did she read during the day?
follow_up_questions: The book has 90 pages. How many pages are left to read?

problem: How many beads did Leila thread after lunch? Before lunch her necklace had 28 beads on it, and by the end of the afternoon it had 73.
follow_up_questions: The finished necklace will have 90 beads. How many beads does it still need?

problem: The bake sale hopes to sell 85 cupcakes. The class sells 38 before lunch and 29 after lunch. How many more cupcakes must they sell to reach the goal?
follow_up_questions: Each cupcake sold for $4. How much money have they raised so far?
They spend $35 on paper plates and napkins. How much of the money is left?
If they sell the cupcakes still needed at $4 each, how much money will they have then?

problem: How many more books do the children need to read to reach their goal of 85 books? For the sponsored read, they read 38 in September and 29 in October.
follow_up_questions: Sponsors pay $4 for each book read. How much money has been raised so far?
The club spends $35 on new bookmarks. How much money is left?
If the children read the missing books, also at $4 each, how much money will the club have then?

problem: A bakery made 36 muffins in the morning and 42 in the afternoon. By closing time 54 muffins had been sold. How many muffins are left?
follow_up_questions: The leftover muffins are packed into boxes of 6. How many boxes are filled?
The next day each box sells for $3. How much money do the boxes bring in?

problem: How many tomatoes are left in the farmer's shed? He picked 36 tomatoes on Monday and 42 on Tuesday, and then sold 54 at the market.
follow_up_questions: He puts the rest into bags of 6. How many bags does he fill?
Each bag sells for $3. How much money will the bags bring in?

problem: Each of the 9 children at the art table got 3 sheets of stickers from the teacher. How many sticker sheets did she give out?
follow_up_questions: By home time the children had used 19 of the sheets. How many sheets were still unused?

problem: The librarian handed out 3 bookmarks to each of nine readers at the story club. Find the number of bookmarks she handed out.
follow_up_questions: By the end, 19 bookmarks had been tucked into books. How many were not yet in a book?

problem: Hina makes 7 paper flowers for her mother, cutting 3 petals for each flower. How many petals does she cut out?
follow_up_questions: Each flower gets 2 green leaves. How many leaves does Hina need?
She cuts 30 leaves from green paper. How many are left over once every flower has its leaves?

problem: How many wheels does Tobias need to build 7 toy tricycles if every tricycle has 3 wheels?
follow_up_questions: Each tricycle also needs 2 pedals. How many pedals does Tobias need?
He has 30 pedals in his parts box. How many pedals will be left over?

problem: Checking each tent at the campsite takes the ranger 6 minutes, and there are 8 tents. A fox watched from the bushes. How long does the ranger spend checking tents?
follow_up_questions: Before the checks she gives a 15-minute safety talk. How many minutes pass from the start of the talk until the checks are done?

problem: How long does it take to braid the hair of 8 dancers if each braid takes 6 minutes? The show's costumes are covered in silver sequins.
follow_up_questions: The braiding starts right after a 15-minute warm-up. How many minutes go by from the start of the warm-up to the last braid?

problem: A greenhouse has six long benches, and each bench holds 9 flower pots. How many flower pots fit on the benches?
How many squares are on a quilt made of six rows with 9 squares in each row?
A kayak locker at the lake costs $4 a day. What does Freya pay to use one for 6 days?
follow_up_questions: She pays with a $50 note. How much change does she get?
She spends $15 of the change on a waterproof bag. How much money does she have left?

problem: For 6 days in a row, Malik borrows a scooter that costs $4 a day to rent. How much does the scooter rental cost him?
follow_up_questions: He hands over a $50 note. What change does he receive?
Then $15 of the change goes on a new bell and lights. How much money is left?

problem: The bakery puts out 8 trays with 5 doughnuts on each. How many doughnuts are ready?
follow_up_questions: By noon, 23 doughnuts have been sold. How many are still on the trays?
Then 4 more trays of 5 doughnuts come out of the kitchen. How many doughnuts are there now?
Each doughnut sells for $2. How much money would selling all of them bring in?

problem: At the garden centre, how many seedlings sit on 8 trays if each tray holds 5 seedlings?
follow_up_questions: Customers buy 23 seedlings in the morning. How many are left?
A worker then brings out 4 more trays of 5 seedlings. How many seedlings are there now?
Every seedling costs $2. How much money would the centre get by selling them all?

problem: Seven tents are set up at the scout camp, and each tent is held down by 6 pegs. How many pegs are holding the tents down?
follow_up_questions: In a storm, 3 pegs snap. How many pegs are still whole?
A new peg costs $4. How much will it cost to replace the snapped pegs?

problem: How many light bulbs are in the seven lamps over the theatre stage if every lamp holds 6 bulbs?
follow_up_questions: During the show 3 bulbs burn out. How many bulbs still work?
A new bulb costs $4. How much will it cost to replace the burnt-out bulbs?

problem: At the beach clean-up, each of the 9 helpers gets a pair of gloves. How many gloves are given out?
How many socks are on the washing line if Mum hangs up 9 pairs of socks?
Lea has a ribbon 8 centimetres long. Her sister's ribbon is 6 times as long. Lea is 3 years younger than her sister. How long is the sister's ribbon?
follow_up_questions: Her sister cuts 5 centimetres off her ribbon to tie a bow. How long is it now?

problem: How long is the banner? Over 3 afternoons, Sami painted a small sign 8 centimetres long and a banner 6 times as long for the bake sale.
follow_up_questions: He trims 5 centimetres off the banner so it fits above the table. How long is the banner now?

problem: Last year the school's garden path was 7 metres long. This year it is 4 times as long. How long is the path now?
follow_up_questions: The fence beside it is 9 metres shorter than the path. How long is the fence?
What is the length of the path and the fence together?
Zoe walks the whole path and then the whole fence, 3 times over. How many metres does she walk?

problem: How long is the swing rope if it is 4 times as long as the 7-foot dog leash hanging in the shed?
follow_up_questions: A clothesline is 9 feet shorter than the swing rope. How long is the clothesline?
What do the swing rope and the clothesline measure together?
Mum buys 3 times that combined length of rope for the new tree house. How many feet of rope does she buy?

problem: Because it was too windy to play outside, the coach opened 4 bags of beanbags with 12 in each bag. How many beanbags were there?
follow_up_questions: The children split 9 of them open while playing. How many beanbags are still in one piece?
The good beanbags are shared equally among 3 teams. How many does each team get?

problem: How many crayons were there when the teacher opened 4 packs of 12 crayons on a snowy day?
follow_up_questions: During art class 9 crayons broke. How many crayons are unbroken?
The unbroken crayons are shared equally among 3 groups. How many does each group get?

problem: For the town fair, volunteers build 3 stalls and use 5 planks of wood for each one. The fair has a pony ride this year. How many planks do they use?
follow_up_questions: They had bought 20 planks. How many planks are left?

problem: How many bags of soil does the garden club use if it fills 3 raised beds with 5 bags each? The club meets behind the library.
follow_up_questions: The club had bought 20 bags. How many bags are still unopened?

problem: The bike shop has 7 crates, and each crate holds 8 wheels. What is the total number of wheels?
follow_up_questions: It turns out 8 of the wheels are bent. How many wheels are fine?
Each go-kart needs 4 good wheels. How many go-karts can be fitted with wheels?
Building one go-kart takes 5 hours. How many hours will all the go-karts take?

problem: Find the number of batteries in 7 packs if there are 8 batteries in each pack.
follow_up_questions: Of those, 8 batteries are dead. How many work?
Each remote-control car needs 4 working batteries. How many cars can be powered?
Each car then drives for 5 hours at the park. How many hours of driving is that altogether?

problem: A teacher opens 3 boxes of building bricks with 32 bricks in each. How many bricks does she tip out onto the carpet?
follow_up_questions: Five bricks slide under the bookcase and are lost. How many bricks are left?

problem: There are 32 cards in each of the 3 new card games the family unwraps. What is the total number of cards?
follow_up_questions: The dog chews up five of the cards. How many cards are left?

problem: At the aquarium, the class watched 4 feeding shows that lasted 12 minutes each. How many minutes did they spend at the shows?
follow_up_questions: Then they spent 25 minutes in the shark tunnel. How long were the shows and the shark tunnel altogether?
The whole visit lasted 90 minutes. How much time was left for lunch?

problem: The quiz night had 4 rounds, and each round took 12 minutes. How long did the rounds take altogether?
follow_up_questions: There was also a 25-minute pizza break. How long did the rounds and the break take together?
The evening lasted 90 minutes. How many minutes were left for handing out prizes?

problem: Each of the 8 classes at Kofi's school planted 3 trees on tree-planting day. How many trees were planted?
How many bird feeders hang in the park if each of its 8 big trees has 3 feeders?
Each loaf that Tariq bakes is cut into 8 slices, and he bakes 6 loaves. How many slices does he have?
follow_up_questions: By evening, 41 slices have been eaten. How many slices are left?

problem: How many muffins can Ilse bake if she fills 6 muffin trays that each hold 8 muffins?
follow_up_questions: Her guests eat 41 muffins. How many muffins remain?

problem: Ana spends 7 minutes on each piano piece and plays 6 pieces. How long does she practise?
follow_up_questions: Her brother Kai practises 15 minutes longer than Ana. How long does he practise?
How many minutes do they practise altogether?

problem: How long does Moses spend reading if he reads 6 short stories and each one takes him 7 minutes?
follow_up_questions: His friend Ruth reads for 15 minutes more than Moses. How long does Ruth read?
What is their combined reading time?

problem: Entry to the science museum costs $3 per child. Mrs. Chen pays for 9 children. How much does she pay?
follow_up_questions: She also buys 3 juice boxes at $2 each. What is her total now?

problem: What do 9 bus tickets cost if each ticket is $3?
follow_up_questions: Dad also picks up 3 newspapers for $2 each. What does he spend in total now?

problem: Leo caught 9 fish at the lake. His aunt caught twice as many. How many fish did his aunt catch?
How many stamps does Noor have if she has twice as many as her brother, who has 9?
A small bag of popcorn at the cinema costs $2. A family-size bucket costs 4 times as much. What is the price of the bucket?
follow_up_questions: Two families each buy a bucket. How much do they spend together?

problem: How much is a jumbo kite if a small kite costs $2 and the jumbo kite costs 4 times as much?
follow_up_questions: Two brothers each buy a jumbo kite. What do they pay altogether?

problem: A teacher has 5 sheets of gold stars with 9 stars on each sheet. How many stars does she have?
follow_up_questions: She gives out 28 stars on Friday. How many are left?
Then she gets 2 more sheets with 9 stars each. How many stars does she have now?

problem: How many stickers does Yara own if she has 5 sticker books with 9 stickers in each?
follow_up_questions: She swaps 28 stickers away at school. How many stickers does she still have?
Her aunt sends her 2 new books with 9 stickers in each. How many stickers does she have now?

problem: Bella's piggy bank holds 30 nickels. How many cents are they worth?
A vending machine at the train station is emptied and gives up 30 nickels. Find their value in cents.
At the school fair, the ticket table has 14 five-dollar bills in its cash box. The fair ends with fireworks. How much money do those bills add up to?
follow_up_questions: There are also 3 ten-dollar bills in the box. What is the total of all these bills?

problem: How much are 14 five-dollar bills worth? A bus driver found them in a lost-property bag. The bag was bright orange.
follow_up_questions: In the same bag he finds 3 ten-dollar bills. What is the total of all the bills?

problem: Bunches of flowers sell for $8 each. On Saturday Amina sells 9 bunches at the market. How much money does she take in?
follow_up_questions: The flowers and paper cost her $25. How much profit did she make on Saturday?
On Sunday she sells 5 bunches at the same price. How much does she take in on Sunday?
Sunday's flowers cost $12. What is her profit for the whole weekend?

problem: How much money does Pedro collect on Saturday by selling 9 birdhouses at $8 each?
follow_up_questions: The wood and nails cost him $25. What is his Saturday profit?
On Sunday he sells 5 birdhouses at the same price. How much does he collect on Sunday?
The supplies for Sunday cost $12. What is his total profit for the weekend?

problem: Mr. Kowalski buys 6 theme park passes at $45 each. What do the passes cost?
follow_up_questions: There is also a $12 parking fee. What is his total bill?
The 6 people in his group split the bill equally. How much does each person pay?

problem: What do 6 train tickets to the seaside cost if each ticket is $45?
follow_up_questions: A $12 seat booking charge is added. What is the total bill?
The 6 travellers share the bill equally. What is each traveller's share?

problem: At the lake, the guide pulls 4 rows of canoes onto the beach, with 10 canoes in each row. How many canoes are there?
follow_up_questions: Each canoe holds 2 paddlers. How many people can paddle at once?

problem: How many bunk beds are there at the summer camp if it has 4 cabins with 10 bunk beds in each?
follow_up_questions: Each bunk bed sleeps 2 campers. How many campers can sleep at the camp?

problem: A sports stadium has 8 sections, and each section has 70 seats. How many seats does the stadium have?
follow_up_questions: At Saturday's match 85 seats are empty. How many fans are watching?
Another 40 fans arrive after half-time. How many fans are in the stadium now?

problem: How many passengers can a train carry if it has 8 carriages and each carriage seats 70 people?
follow_up_questions: On Monday morning 85 seats are empty. How many passengers are on board?
At the next station 40 more passengers get on and find seats. How many passengers are on the train now?

problem: For the school picnic, the cook cuts 8 trays of cornbread into 10 squares each. How many squares is that?
follow_up_questions: The children eat 66 squares. How many squares are left over?

problem: How many orange segments are there if Aunt Ruth peels 8 oranges and each orange has 10 segments?
follow_up_questions: The football team eats 66 segments at half-time. How many are left?

While tidying the craft room, a teacher found 28 paintbrushes. She sorted them equally into 4 jars. How many brushes went into each jar?
follow_up_questions: She then takes 3 brushes from one jar for a project. How many brushes are in that jar now?

problem: How many screws go in each tray if a carpenter sorts 28 screws equally into 4 trays?
follow_up_questions: He takes 3 screws from one tray to fix a shelf. How many screws are left in that tray?

problem: The class is covering a bulletin board with square paper tiles. The board is 9 feet long and 5 feet wide, and each tile is 1 foot on a side. How many tiles will cover the board?
follow_up_questions: Each tile costs 2 dollars. How much do all the tiles cost?
The class budget for the board is 95 dollars. How much will be left after buying the tiles?

problem: How many square mats, each 1 metre on a side, will cover a gym floor area that is 9 metres long and 5 metres wide?
follow_up_questions: Cleaning one mat costs 2 dollars. How much will cleaning all of them cost?
The cleaning budget is 95 dollars. How much will be left after cleaning the mats?

problem: Each bookmark for the reading fair uses 3 inches of ribbon. Mrs. Popescu has a ribbon 75 inches long. How many bookmarks can she make at most?
follow_up_questions: There are 30 children in the class, and each one needs a bookmark. How many more bookmarks does she need?

problem: How many name tags can be cut from a strip of card 75 centimetres long if each tag is 3 centimetres wide?
follow_up_questions: There are 30 guests, and each one needs a tag. How many more tags are needed?

problem: Each week, Tunde reads 35 pages of his adventure book. If he keeps this up, how many pages will he read in 8 weeks?
follow_up_questions: His sister reads 45 pages fewer than him over those weeks. How many pages does she read?
How many pages did the two of them read together?
The library gives a sticker for every 5 pages. How many stickers does his sister earn?

problem: How many points will a bowling team score in 8 games if it averages 35 points a game?
follow_up_questions: Their rivals finish those games 45 points behind them. What is the rivals' score?
How many points did the two teams score together?
The alley gives a free drink voucher for every 5 points. How many vouchers do the rivals earn?

problem: A garden hose sprays 45 litres of water each minute. Grandpa waters the lawn for 8 minutes. How many litres of water does he use?
How many litres of milk flow into the tank in 8 minutes if the milking machine pumps 45 litres a minute?
On a Saturday morning, a hairdresser has 6 children waiting for haircuts. Each haircut takes her 9 minutes. How long will all the haircuts take?
follow_up_questions: She also spends 15 minutes sweeping the floor. How many minutes does she work in all?
Her morning shift is 90 minutes long. How much time is left for other jobs?

problem: How many minutes does it take a vet to vaccinate 6 puppies if each one takes 9 minutes?
follow_up_questions: She also spends 15 minutes writing notes. How many minutes does she work in all?
She has 90 minutes before lunch. How much time is left over?

problem: Leila gives her hamster 4 sunflower seeds each day. How many seeds does she use in a week?
follow_up_questions: A bag of seeds holds 56 seeds. How many weeks will a bag last?

problem: How many vitamin drops does a zookeeper use in a week if she adds 4 drops to the parrot's water each day?
follow_up_questions: One bottle holds 56 drops. How many weeks will a bottle last?

problem: The apple orchard picked 72 crates of apples. They were loaded onto 4 trucks, with the same number of crates on each. How many crates went on each truck?
follow_up_questions: Each crate weighs 5 kilograms. How heavy is the load on one truck?
One truck also takes 6 crates of pears that weigh 4 kilograms each. How heavy is its load now?

problem: How many sacks of rice does each of 4 boats carry if 72 sacks are shared equally among them?
follow_up_questions: Each sack weighs 5 kilograms. How much rice is on one boat?
One boat also loads 6 sacks of beans weighing 4 kilograms each. How heavy is its load now?

problem: Kayode has 90 cents to spend at the school fair. Lollipops cost 6 cents each, and he wants as many as he can buy. How many lollipops can he buy?
follow_up_questions: He gives a third of his lollipops to his sister. How many lollipops does his sister get?

problem: How many stickers can Dana buy with 90 cents if each sticker costs 6 cents?
follow_up_questions: She gives a third of them to her best friend. How many stickers does her friend get?

problem: The garden centre delivered 7 bags of soil to the school garden, and each bag holds 9 scoops. By afternoon the children had used 25 scoops to fill flower pots. How many scoops of soil are left?
follow_up_questions: The next morning 2 more bags of the same size arrive. How many scoops are there now?
Each tree planter needs 8 scoops of soil. How many planters can the children fill?
The garden needs 10 planters. How many more planters still need soil?

problem: How many cups of flour are left in the bakery? A supplier delivered 7 tins holding 9 cups each, and the baker has already used 25 cups.
follow_up_questions: The next day 2 more tins of the same size arrive. How many cups of flour are there now?
Each loaf of bread needs 8 cups of flour. How many loaves can the baker make?
The baker has 10 orders for loaves. How many orders cannot be filled?

problem: In the dance class, pupils practise the waltz in pairs. Today 46 pupils have come. How many pairs will be on the dance floor?
follow_up_questions: The teacher needs one number card for each pair and already has 15 cards. How many more cards does she need?

problem: How many canoes are needed for 46 campers if they paddle in pairs, one pair per canoe?
follow_up_questions: The camp has 15 canoes ready at the dock. How many more canoes does it need?

problem: Selin has collected 37 stickers on her reading chart. She gets a prize once she has 65 stickers. How many more stickers does she need?
follow_up_questions: She earns 4 stickers every day she reads at home. How many days of reading does she need to get the stickers she still needs?

problem: How many more shells does Nikolai need to find? His collection has 37 shells, and he wants it to reach 65.
follow_up_questions: He finds 4 shells on each walk along the beach. How many walks will it take him to find the shells he still needs?

problem: Apple-picking season had begun, and a farmer filled 27 crates in the orchard. Each crate held 10 apples. What is the total number of apples picked?
follow_up_questions: The farmer puts them into bags of 9. How many bags can he fill?
Each bag sells for 7 dollars. How much money will he make if he sells them all?

problem: How many pencils came in the delivery if the school received 27 boxes with 10 pencils in each box?
follow_up_questions: The secretary sorts them into cups of 9. How many cups does she fill?
Each cup of pencils sells at the school shop for 7 dollars. How much money would selling all the cups bring in?

problem: On Saturday a farm gave 91 apples to the school instead of letting them go to waste. The school shares them equally among 7 classes. How many apples does each class receive?
follow_up_questions: One class cuts each of its apples in half for a snack. How many halves does it have?
At snack time, 19 halves are eaten. How many halves are left?
The teacher brings 14 more halves the next day. How many halves does the class have then?

problem: How many oranges does each of 7 football teams get when a market stall gives away 91 oranges equally?
follow_up_questions: One team cuts each of its oranges in half. How many halves does it have?
During the match, the players eat 19 halves. How many halves remain?
A parent brings 14 more halves. How many halves does the team have now?

problem: Haruki took 40 dollars to the water park. The entry ticket cost 15 dollars, and later he spent 9 dollars on ice cream and a drink. How much money did he bring home?
follow_up_questions: At home, his mum gives him 5 dollars for washing the dishes. How much does he have now?
He puts a third of it in his savings box. How much goes in the box?
How much does he keep in his wallet?

problem: How much money did Sara have left after a day at the museum? She started with 40 dollars, paid 15 dollars to get in and spent 9 dollars in the gift shop.
follow_up_questions: Her aunt then gives her 5 dollars. How much does she have now?
She saves a third of it in her piggy bank. How much does she save?
How much is left to spend?

problem: For the big match at the stadium, fans arrived on 6 trains with 42 people on each one. How many fans came by train?
follow_up_questions: Of them, 52 got to meet the players. How many did not?
Those who did not meet the players toured the stadium in groups of 40. How many groups were there?

problem: How many children went to the zoo if 6 school buses each carried 42 children?
follow_up_questions: Of them, 52 fed the giraffes. How many did not?
The children who did not feed the giraffes watched the penguin show in groups of 40. How many groups were there?

problem: Each rowing boat at the lake holds four people. On the busiest afternoon, all 23 boats were out on the water and full. How many people were rowing?
follow_up_questions: Later, 17 people return to shore. How many are still on the water?

problem: How many guests are seated at the wedding if there are 23 round tables and four guests sit at each one?
follow_up_questions: During the speeches, 17 guests step outside. How many are still at the tables?

problem: Each of the 12 apple trees in the school orchard has seven apples left on it. What is the total number of apples on those trees?
follow_up_questions: A class picks 29 of them. How many apples are left on the trees?
The caretaker then picks 25 more for the kitchen. How many are left now?
He packs the rest into boxes of 6. How many boxes does he fill?

problem: How many eggs are in the henhouse if each of its 12 nesting boxes holds seven eggs?
follow_up_questions: The farmer collects 29 eggs for breakfast. How many eggs are left?
Then she takes 25 more to sell. How many are left now?
She puts the rest into cartons of 6. How many cartons does she fill?

problem: On the class trip to the farm, each of the 26 pupils collected 3 eggs from the henhouse. How many eggs did the pupils collect?
How many balloons were blown up at the party if every one of the 26 guests blew up 3?
The craft club bought 18 packs of googly eyes, and each pack came with twelve eyes. How many googly eyes did the club get?
follow_up_questions: The children make monsters with 4 eyes each. How many monsters can they make?

problem: How many pencils does the class have if it got 18 boxes with 12 pencils in each?
follow_up_questions: Each pupil gets 4 pencils. How many pupils get pencils?

problem: A farmer is fencing a goat pen shaped like a hexagon. Each of its six sides is 7 metres long. How much fencing does she need?
follow_up_questions: Fencing comes in rolls of 6 metres. How many rolls does she need?

problem: How far does Ines walk if she goes once around a six-sided pond path and every side is 7 metres long?
follow_up_questions: Fairy lights are sold in strings of 6 metres. How many strings are needed to light the whole path?
